cards.text: Fourth concept on the GLP-1 stasis angle, mechanism-forward. cards.title: REVISION LOG · 2026-08-25
cards.text:
1. Ad 02 opened 'CELERY JUICE ='. Brooks: use CELERY. The ingredient word is now identical on all three, which also makes the set read as one campaign rather than three one-offs.

2. Headlines on all three sat too close to the left and right edges. Re-rendered with a hard margin rule.

MARGIN RULE, learned the hard way twice now. 'Inset from the edges with a clear band on both sides' is too soft and fails silently: the type still renders nearly full-bleed. The wording that actually works is an explicit fraction plus permission to shrink the type: no letter comes closer to either edge than one fifth of the image width, size the type down so every line fits comfortably inside those margins. Use that phrasing on every headline-heavy static from here on.

cards.title: WHY 5 DAYS AND NOT 9
cards.text:
The reference says 9 days. That number is theirs and it is arbitrary.

The only figure defensible for Motilli is 5, from the mechanism bible: 'First normal, non-cramping movement often around day five.'

Anything larger would have to be invented, which breaks Law 2. Running 5 honestly beats inflating to match the reference.

cards.title: SHARED PRIMARY TEXT
cards.text:
That is what a stalled colon looks like on film.

If you are on a GLP-1, the medication is doing exactly what it was designed to do. It slows digestion down. The trouble is the slowdown reaches all the way to the end.

Your colon is a muscle. It only contracts when it gets a signal, and that signal is a short-chain fatty acid called butyrate that the bacteria in your colon make out of the fiber that reaches them. Slow everything down, less reaches them, the colony thins out, and the signal fades. What stays behind is what you are looking at on the left.

Celery is in this for one thing. A compound called apigenin, which celery juice is concentrated in, and which barely absorbs into your bloodstream. In most supplements that would be a flaw. Here it is the entire point, because it means the apigenin stays down in the colon where the problem actually is, calming the lining and shifting the balance back toward the bacteria that make butyrate.

Motilli is concentrated celery juice standardized for a real dose of that apigenin, plus a fine soluble fiber to feed those bacteria once they come back. Rebuild the place, then feed what grows there.

The first few days are quiet, because this is not a laxative and nothing is being forced. The first normal, non-cramping movement usually lands around day five. From there it stops being the thing you build your morning around.

None of this touches your weight loss. Weight loss lives in the brain and the appetite. This lives in the colon and the bacteria in it. Two separate systems, so you rebuild one and stay on the other.

Two gummies before bed with a full glass of water. Sixty in a bottle. Third-party tested, lab results posted.

Ninety days to decide. Email inside ninety days and every dollar comes back, no return required.

cards.title: TWO DELIBERATE DEVIATIONS FROM THE REFERENCE
cards.text:
1. ONE VIEW ACROSS BOTH FILMS. The reference pairs a lateral left panel with a frontal right panel. Different views of different things is not a before and after. Ours holds the same frontal AP view, same framing, same scale, on both sides. More credible, not less.

2. DISCLAIMER ADDED. The reference runs none. On a before/after medical-imagery results claim the small grey line is worth having, and there is dead black space for it.

NO JAR, matching the reference. This format's power is that it looks like evidence rather than an ad. A jar variant sitting in the black space below the panels is one pass away if you want brand attribution on the creative.

cards.title: FRAME QA · all three, re-verified after the fix
cards.text:
Headline margins: PASS. Clear black band on both sides of every line in all three, no letter near an edge.

Ingredient word: PASS. CELERY on all three, no CELERY JUICE anywhere on the creative.

Headline: PASS. White upright first line, lime bold italic outcome lines, spelled exactly.

Labels: PASS. BEFORE and AFTER in white bold caps, each over its own panel.

Films: PASS. Two panels, same view and scale, thin white divider. Left loaded through every loop with dense material, bowel widened, almost no gas space. Right clear with clean dark gas pattern, spine and pelvis crisp. Difference obvious at a glance.

Disclaimer: PASS. Present in all three.

No invented words, badges, prices, percentages, watermarks, dates or patient names anywhere on the films.

cards.title: AUDIT
cards.text:
Law 2: no invented study, percentage, doctor, review count or customer quote. The 5-day marker traces to the mechanism bible. The apigenin description uses the bible's own phrasing ('concentrated in celery juice', 'barely absorbs') rather than a superlative like 'richest food source', which is not sourced anywhere in the folder.

Law 9: clean through lawgate.

Two separate systems: present.

Swap test: PASS. Apigenin staying in the colon and the rebuild-then-feed order are ours. Drop a laxative into this ad and the copy argues against it.

Shelf life: evergreen.

CLAIM RISK, HIGHEST OF THE FOUR CONCEPTS. A before/after X-ray is medical-imagery evidence for a supplement. The films are generated, not real patient scans, and the copy never claims otherwise, but the format implies clinical documentation. 'CLEARED OUT IN 5 DAYS' over an X-ray is the strongest promise in the account. Get a compliance read before this one spends.

VERIFY BEFORE LAUNCH: the 90-day no-return-required guarantee wording against the live policy page.
